1.en: Whoever strives shall find, and whoever sows shall reap.

2.en: Resolve comes in the measure of those who hold it, and noble deeds in the measure of the noble.

3.en: If you venture after a lofty honor, settle for nothing less than the stars.

4.en: Whoever fears to climb the mountains will live forever among the pits.

5.en: Goals are not won by wishing; the world is taken by striving.

6.en: Heights are gained in the measure of toil; whoever seeks the summit must keep the night awake.

7.en: A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.

8.en: It does not matter how slowly you go, as long as you do not stop.

9.en: If you can't fly, then run; if you can't run, then walk; if you can't walk, then crawl; but whatever you do, you have to keep moving forward.

10.en: You don't have to be great to start, but you have to start to be great.

11.en: Do what you can, with what you have, where you are.

12.en: Whether you think you can, or you think you can't, you're right.

13.en: The way to get started is to quit talking and begin doing.

14.en: Be the change you wish to see in the world.

15.en: Whatever the mind can conceive and believe, it can achieve.

16.en: Fear does not prevent death; it prevents life.

17.en: If you add nothing to the world, you are yourself a surplus to it.

18.en: Nothing scratches your skin like your own nail, so take charge of all your affairs yourself.
18.note_en: Rely on yourself, for no one tends to your needs as well as you do.

20.en: Every diligent person has a share.

21.en: Do not put off today's work until tomorrow.

22.en: The mind is the mightiest weapon.

23.en: Success is the sum of small efforts, repeated day in and day out.

24.en: The only way to do great work is to love what you do.

25.en: I have not failed; I've just found ten thousand ways that won't work.

26.en: Genius is one percent inspiration and ninety-nine percent perspiration.

27.en: It always seems impossible until it's done.

28.en: Discipline is the bridge between goals and accomplishment.

29.en: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.

30.en: Luck is what happens when preparation meets opportunity.

31.en: It takes twenty years to build a reputation and five minutes to ruin it.

33.en: Learn more from failure than you learn from success.

34.en: Time is like a sword: if you do not cut it, it will cut you.
34.note_en: Use your time well, or it will be lost to your cost.

35.en: In patience lies safety, and in haste lies regret.

36.en: The first of the rain is a single drop.
36.note_en: Great things grow from small beginnings.

37.en: People don't buy what you do; they buy why you do it.

38.en: Not all that a man desires does he attain; the winds blow as the ships would not wish.

39.en: Let the days do as they will, and be at peace when fate decrees.

40.en: Nations live only as long as their morals endure; when their morals are gone, they are gone.

41.en: Be beautiful, and you will see the world as beautiful.

42.en: Each person's worth lies in what they do well.
42.author_en: Attributed to Ali ibn Abi Talib

43.en: The vanquished are forever eager to imitate the victor.

44.en: Your children are not your children. They are the sons and daughters of Life's longing for itself.

45.en: The unexamined life is not worth living.

46.en: Life is like riding a bicycle: to keep your balance, you must keep moving.

47.en: Yesterday I was clever, so I wanted to change the world. Today I am wise, so I am changing myself.

48.en: Nothing is more powerful than an idea whose time has come.

49.en: The best speech is brief and to the point.

50.en: If speech is silver, then silence is golden.

51.en: An ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure.

52.en: Many a harm brings hidden good.
52.note_en: Misfortune can turn out to be a blessing in disguise.

53.en: A sound mind in a sound body.

54.en: If you are not part of the solution, you are part of the problem.

55.en: Alone we can do so little; together we can do so much.

56.en: The noblest place on earth is the saddle of a swift horse, and the best companion in any age is a book.

57.en: Rise for the teacher and give him full honor; the teacher is almost a messenger.

58.en: Education, like water and air, is the right of every human being.

59.en: Imagination is more important than knowledge.

60.en: Education is the most powerful weapon which you can use to change the world.

61.en: Education is the passport to the future, for tomorrow belongs to those who prepare for it today.

62.en: If I have seen further, it is by standing on the shoulders of giants.

63.en: Nothing in life is to be feared, it is only to be understood. Now is the time to understand more, so that we may fear less.

64.en: An investment in knowledge pays the best interest.

65.en: The roots of education are bitter, but the fruit is sweet.

66.en: A little knowledge that acts is worth infinitely more than much knowledge that is idle.

67.en: Learning in youth is like carving in stone.
67.note_en: What is learned when young stays for life.

68.en: Seek knowledge from the cradle to the grave.

69.en: I soothe my soul with hopes I watch for; how narrow life would be, were it not for the wide space of hope.

70.en: It grew tight, and when its rings closed fast, it opened, though I thought it never would.

71.en: If, one day, a people wills to live, then fate must surely answer.

72.en: Optimism is the faith that leads to achievement.

73.en: Patience is the key to relief.

74.en: Tighten, O hardship, and you will break open.
74.note_en: When a crisis reaches its worst, relief is near.

75.en: After hardship comes ease, and after the night rises the dawn.

76.en: Every sunrise gives you a new chance to begin again.

77.en: A leader is one who knows the way, goes the way, and shows the way.

78.en: Management is doing things right; leadership is doing the right things.

79.en: There is nothing so useless as doing efficiently that which should not be done at all.

80.en: Innovation distinguishes between a leader and a follower.

81.en: The master of a people is their servant.
81.note_en: True leadership means serving those you lead.

82.en: The most dangerous phrase in the language is: We've always done it this way.

83.en: The best way to predict the future is to invent it.

84.en: Any sufficiently advanced technology is indistinguishable from magic.

85.en: The most profound technologies are those that disappear; they weave themselves into the fabric of everyday life until they are indistinguishable from it.

86.en: Talk is cheap. Show me the code.

87.en: Simplicity is a prerequisite for reliability.

88.en: Your most unhappy customers are your greatest source of learning.

90.en: Technology is a tool; it is people who give it meaning.

92.en: AI is one of the most profound things we're working on as humanity, more profound than fire or electricity.

93.en: Our success in creating AI could be the biggest event in the history of our civilization, or the worst.

94.en: There is nothing artificial about AI. It is inspired by people, created by people, and, most importantly, it impacts people.

95.en: The question of whether machines can think is no more interesting than the question of whether submarines can swim.

96.en: We can only see a short distance ahead, but we can see plenty there that needs to be done.

97.en: AI will not replace you, but someone who masters it might.

99.en: The media is the most powerful entity on earth. It has the power to make the innocent guilty and the guilty innocent.

100.en: The media either builds awareness or washes it away.

101.en: The media is the instrument of a society's awareness.

102.en: Verify before you share, for every word is a trust.

103.en: The one standing on the shore is always a fine swimmer.
103.note_en: It is easy to judge and advise when you are not the one facing the hardship.

104.en: The camel never sees the crook in its own neck.
104.note_en: People notice others' faults but are blind to their own.

105.en: Hand joined to hand throws far.
105.note_en: Together people achieve what no one can achieve alone.

106.en: The pen does not cure dullness.
106.note_en: Schooling alone cannot give a person good sense.

107.en: Lose a third of your wealth rather than all of it.
107.note_en: Accept a partial loss to save yourself from total ruin.

108.en: Mourning is led by the family of the departed.
108.note_en: Those a matter concerns most must care for it most and take the lead.

109.en: A shameful deed is always disowned.
109.note_en: No one willingly admits to a disgraceful act.

110.en: Do not hand the ladle to one who does not know how to serve.
110.note_en: Entrust a task only to someone capable of doing it.

111.note_en: Recovery and improvement come gradually, so be patient.

112.en: What the goat does to the qarad tree, she will find on her own hide.
112.note_en: The goat eats the qarad pods that are later used to tan her skin: what you do comes back to you.

113.en: Drag the thorns across a hide that is not your own.
113.note_en: People are careless with what does not belong to them and do not feel another's pain.

114.en: A letter's address tells you enough of its contents.
114.note_en: First signs are often enough to reveal the whole matter.

115.en: In his mother's eyes, the monkey is a gazelle.

116.en: Though I come last in time, I shall bring what the ancients could not.

117.en: No goal stays out of reach for a people whose steed is daring.

118.en: Were it not for hardship, all men would be lords: generosity brings poverty, and daring brings death.

119.en: Fear is only what a man chooses to fear, and safety only what he deems safe.

120.en: Be patient and you will attain.

122.en: What cannot be attained in full should not be abandoned in full.

123.en: Better to arrive late than never to arrive.

124.note_en: Action and effort bring reward, while idleness brings nothing.

125.en: Knowing is not enough; we must apply. Willing is not enough; we must do.

126.en: He who has a why to live can bear almost any how.

127.en: The man who moves a mountain begins by carrying away small stones.

128.en: Anyone who has never made a mistake has never tried anything new.

129.en: You don't have to see the whole staircase, just take the first step.

130.en: Every morning is a blank page, so write on it something worth reading.

131.en: Do not wait for perfect conditions; begin with what is in your hands, and the road will widen.

132.en: Dreams do not come true by sleeping, but by waking up for them every day.

133.en: Your time is limited, so don't waste it living someone else's life.

134.en: You can't connect the dots looking forward; you can only connect them looking backward.

135.en: The most important investment you can make is in yourself.

136.en: We always overestimate the change that will occur in the next two years and underestimate the change that will occur in the next ten.

137.en: One never notices what has been done; one can only see what remains to be done.

138.en: Every steed may stumble, and every scholar may err.

140.en: Every delay holds some hidden good.

141.en: No right is ever lost while someone still demands it.

142.en: A little that lasts is better than much that ceases.

143.en: Success is not a station you reach, but a way you travel.

144.en: Failure is not the opposite of success, but part of it.

145.en: The days will reveal to you what you did not know, and news will come to you from one you never sent to seek it.

146.en: Whatever trait a man may hold, though he thinks it hidden from people, it will become known.

147.en: A man's tongue is half of him, his heart the other half; what remains is but a form of flesh and blood.

148.en: We blame our times, yet the fault lies within us; our times have no fault but us.

149.en: When the fool speaks, do not answer him; silence is better than a reply.

150.en: The eye of approval is blind to every fault, but the eye of resentment lays every flaw bare.

151.en: When you see the lion's fangs bared, do not think the lion is smiling.

152.en: One whose mouth is bitter with sickness finds even pure, sweet water bitter.

153.en: The man of reason suffers amid bliss because of his mind, while the ignorant one lives in bliss amid misery.

154.en: People are enemies of what they do not know.
154.author_en: Attributed to Ali ibn Abi Talib

155.en: May God have mercy on the one who shows me my faults as a gift.

156.en: It is not things that disturb people, but their judgments about them.

157.en: We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.

158.en: He who knows others is clever; he who knows himself is wise.

159.en: Everyone thinks of changing the world, but no one thinks of changing himself.

161.en: All that glitters is not gold.

162.en: Once the cause is known, the wonder fades.

163.en: Every vessel seeps with what it holds.
163.note_en: A person's words and deeds reveal what lies within them.

164.en: Ask one who has experienced, not one who is merely wise.
164.note_en: Practical experience is a better guide than theory.

165.en: Necessity is the mother of invention.

166.en: A sparrow in the hand is better than ten on the tree.

167.en: What one grows up on, one grows old on.
167.note_en: Habits formed in youth stay with a person for life.

168.en: Every occasion has its fitting words.

169.en: The sword has outrun the reproach.
169.note_en: The deed is already done, and blame now comes too late.

170.note_en: Said of one whose own actions cause their downfall.

171.en: Tomorrow is near for the one who watches for it.
171.note_en: What is awaited will soon come and reveal the truth.

172.en: The eye sees far, but the hand is short.
172.note_en: One can see what one wants but lacks the means to reach it.

173.en: The people of Mecca know its mountain paths best.
173.note_en: Those who live with a matter understand it best.

174.en: The best of matters is the middle way.

175.en: No one who seeks counsel comes to regret.

176.en: A day for you, and a day against you.

177.en: They planted and we ate; we plant so that others may eat.

178.en: A book is read from its title.
178.note_en: The outward signs of a thing reveal much about its substance.

179.en: When a thing exceeds its limit, it turns into its opposite.

181.en: Injustice heralds the ruin of civilization.

182.en: Ignorance leads to fear, fear leads to hatred, and hatred leads to violence.

183.en: I am the sea, with pearls hidden in its depths; have they asked the diver about my shells?

184.en: Leave your homeland in pursuit of greatness, and travel, for in travel lie five benefits.

185.en: Whoever studies the books of science, if his aim is to know the truth, must make himself an adversary of everything he reads.

186.en: Knowledge is light, and ignorance is darkness.

187.en: The bane of knowledge is forgetting.

188.en: The first principle is that you must not fool yourself, and you are the easiest person to fool.

189.en: Science is more a way of thinking than a body of knowledge.

190.en: He who learns but does not think is lost; he who thinks but does not learn is in danger.

191.en: Reading is to the mind what exercise is to the body.

192.en: Every book you read is a new window through which you look out on the world.

193.en: A good question is half of knowledge.

194.en: On this earth there is what makes life worth living.

195.en: Even the darkest night will end, and the sun will rise.

196.en: Darkness cannot drive out darkness; only light can do that. Hate cannot drive out hate; only love can do that.

197.en: Everything can be taken from a man but one thing: the freedom to choose his attitude in any given set of circumstances.

198.en: I learned that courage was not the absence of fear, but the triumph over it.

199.en: He said: The sky is gloomy, and he frowned. I said: Smile; the gloom in the sky is enough.

200.en: Many a calamity leaves a man at his wits' end, yet with God lies the way out.

201.en: After the clouds, the sun shines.

202.en: However long the night, the dawn must come.

203.en: A seed does not see the sun in its first days, yet it grows toward it.

204.en: Hardship tightens only so that it may give way to relief.
204.note_en: When things are at their hardest, relief is near.

205.en: A leader is best when people barely know he exists; when his work is done, they will say: we did it ourselves.

206.en: Leadership is the art of getting someone else to do something you want done because he wants to do it.

207.en: Lead from the back, and let others believe they are in front.

208.en: Sound judgment comes before the courage of the brave; it comes first, and courage takes second place.

209.en: Choose the companion before the road.
209.note_en: Pick your company carefully before setting out on any journey or venture.

212.en: A true leader makes leaders, not followers.

213.en: Any fool can write code that a computer can understand. Good programmers write code that humans can understand.

214.en: Premature optimization is the root of all evil in programming.

215.en: Make it work, make it right, make it fast.

216.en: The Analytical Engine weaves algebraic patterns just as the loom weaves flowers and leaves.

218.en: Technology that does not serve people becomes a burden on them.

219.en: If a typical person can do a mental task with less than one second of thought, we can probably automate it using AI either now or in the near future.

220.en: As soon as it works, no one calls it AI anymore.

221.en: A good question to AI is half the answer.

222.en: The machine memorizes, and the human understands; so be the one who understands.

223.en: If liberty means anything at all, it means the right to tell people what they do not want to hear.

224.en: The bane of news is those who relay it.
224.note_en: News is distorted most by the people who pass it on.

225.en: A lie flies, while the truth walks on foot.

226.en: Not all that is known should be said, and not all that is said has found its time.

227.en: A friend in need is a friend indeed.

228.en: Tell me who your companions are, and I will tell you who you are.

229.en: Many a brother of yours was not born of your mother.
229.note_en: A true friend can be as close as a blood brother.

230.en: Choose the neighbor before the house.
230.note_en: A good neighbor matters more than the home itself.

231.en: Solitude is better than bad company.

232.en: Out of sight, out of mind.

233.en: Farewell to the world if it holds no true friend, faithful to his word and fair.

234.en: If a man cares for you only out of obligation, let him go, and do not grieve over him too much.

235.en: A friend is a single soul dwelling in two bodies.

236.en: I would rather walk with a friend in the dark than alone in the light.

237.en: A true friend sees the pain in your eyes while others believe your smile.

238.en: No nation's edifice stands firm when its morals lie in ruins.

239.en: The soundness of your affairs rests on character; so set your soul right by virtue, and you will stand upright.

240.en: Honor the noble and you win him over; honor the base and he grows insolent.

241.en: Injustice from one's own kin cuts deeper than the blow of a sharp Indian sword.

242.en: Since when have you enslaved people when their mothers bore them free?

243.en: Do not be the slave of another when God has made you free.
243.author_en: Attributed to Ali ibn Abi Talib

244.en: If it is not right, do not do it; if it is not true, do not say it.

245.en: The weak can never forgive; forgiveness is the attribute of the strong.

246.en: Your tongue is your steed: guard it and it guards you; betray it and it betrays you.

247.en: Whoever digs a pit for his brother falls into it.

248.en: As you judge, so shall you be judged.

249.en: Whoever feels safe from punishment forgets his manners.

250.en: Generosity comes from what one has.
250.note_en: Give within your means; no one is expected to give what they do not have.

251.en: It is when you give of yourself that you truly give.

252.en: Character is measured not by what you say, but by what you do when no one is watching.

253.en: Contentment is a treasure that never runs out.

254.en: Whoever watches people dies of worry.
254.note_en: Constantly comparing yourself to others or fretting over their opinions only brings misery.

255.en: O you who complain while nothing ails you, how will you be when real illness comes?

256.en: One whose soul holds no beauty sees nothing beautiful in all existence.

257.en: Our life is what our thoughts make it.

259.en: Happiness is not something ready-made; it comes from your own actions.

260.en: The best and most beautiful things in the world cannot be seen or even touched; they must be felt with the heart.

261.en: Wealth consists not in having great possessions, but in having few wants.

262.en: Happiness is rejoicing in what you have, not grieving over what you lack.

263.en: Your smile to the morning is the first gift you give yourself.

264.en: The beats of a man's heart keep telling him: life is but minutes and seconds.

265.en: O son of Adam, you are nothing but days; whenever a day passes, a part of you is gone.

266.en: It is not that we have a short time to live, but that we waste a great deal of it.

268.en: Time is breaths that never return.

269.en: Work in silence, and let your success make the noise.

270.en: An hour of planning saves you days of toil.

271.en: The early morning carries the blessing of the whole day.

272.en: A mother is a school: prepare her well, and you prepare a people of noble roots.

273.en: All that I am, or hope to be, I owe to my mother.

274.en: A home is not walls, but the hearts that dwell within it.

275.en: Honoring your parents is a debt you repay to them, and a loan your children will repay to you.

276.en: Family is where life begins and love never ends.

601.en: Every line of code is a promise to someone you have not met yet.
601.note_en: What a developer writes today reaches strangers tomorrow, so it should be written with the care of a promise.

602.en: Success is not having your app downloaded; it is having it missed when it is gone.
602.note_en: A product's real value is the place it holds in people's lives, not its download numbers.

603.en: Stored knowledge is still water; it gives life to nothing until it flows between people.
603.note_en: Knowledge locked in files and minds helps no one; it comes alive when it is shared.

604.en: Data is memory, knowledge is understanding, and impact is what we make of both.
604.note_en: Collecting data is not enough; it must become understanding, then action that leaves a mark.

605.en: Design is respect for the time of someone who will never thank you for it.
605.note_en: Good design goes unnoticed; it saves people effort they never knew they were spared.

606.en: Measure technology by the time it gives back to you, not by the time it takes.
606.note_en: Useful technology frees time for what matters; technology that only consumes it is a loss, however dazzling.

607.en: A screen is a window; if it does not open onto something better, close it.
607.note_en: A call to use screens mindfully: stay while they enrich your life, leave when they drain it.

608.en: The first version is never perfect, but only the first version can teach you what perfect means.
608.note_en: Don't wait for perfection to start; shipping and learning is the only way to know what people really need.

609.en: A product that does not listen to its users ends up talking to itself.
609.note_en: Listening to users is what keeps a product alive and useful; without it, the audience leaves.

610.en: A good product answers the question; a great product makes the question unnecessary.
610.note_en: The greatest products understand a need before the person has to ask.

611.en: Whoever owns knowledge owns yesterday; whoever manages it well owns tomorrow.
611.note_en: Owning knowledge alone does not shape the future; the future belongs to those who organize, share and use it well.

612.en: Don't look for an idea no one has had; look for a pain no one has listened to.
612.note_en: Great products are born from understanding real struggles, not from chasing novelty for its own sake.

613.en: A machine answers in a moment; wisdom takes a lifetime to know what to ask.
613.note_en: Fast answers are no substitute for wisdom; knowing the right question is the fruit of long experience.

614.en: Knowledge is no longer scarce; what is rare today is knowing what to do with it.
614.note_en: In an age of abundant knowledge, value shifts from having information to using it well.

615.en: Teach the machine to calculate, and teach yourself to choose.
615.note_en: Calculation can be delegated to machines; choice and judgment remain a human responsibility.

616.en: AI is a mirror: it shows you the minds of its makers before it shows you its own.
616.note_en: What intelligent systems do reflects the values and data of their makers, so fixing them starts with us.

617.en: Fearing the machine will not protect us; understanding it better than it understands us will.
617.note_en: The path to living safely with AI is knowledge and understanding, not panic.

618.en: The model learns from our data, so let us be a lesson worth learning.
618.note_en: What we write and publish today becomes what machines learn from, so let it be useful and true.

619.en: Give the machine the tasks; keep the meaning for yourself.
619.note_en: Let AI carry the repetitive work, and keep for yourself what gives your work and life their worth.

620.en: When machines are equally intelligent, what sets them apart is the conscience that guides them.
620.note_en: Technical power will be available to all; the real difference lies in the ethics of those who build and use it.

621.en: Knowledge a machine generates and no human verifies is elegant noise.
621.note_en: AI output needs a critical human mind to verify it before it can count as knowledge.

622.en: The machine will write faster than you, but it will never know whom you are writing for.
622.note_en: Speed is the machine's gift; knowing the reader and speaking to their heart remains a human one.

623.en: The smartest system is the one that makes people smarter, not lazier.
623.note_en: AI should be judged by what it adds to human abilities, not by what it lets wither.

624.en: AI will multiply knowledge; let our task be to multiply wisdom.
624.note_en: An abundance of information only deepens our need for the wisdom to tell what matters and use it well.

625.en: A leader lights the way not to be seen, but so that others can see.
625.note_en: Leadership is service and clarity for the team, not a display of oneself.

626.en: Building a product is hard; building the people who build it with you is leadership.
626.note_en: A leader's greatest creation is not the product itself, but the team able to build and grow it.

627.en: A leader's strength is measured not by what they know, but by what their team knows because of them.
627.note_en: A true leader shares knowledge rather than hoarding it, so the team grows and its capacity with it.

628.en: When you are wrong, say so; those words build trust faster than a thousand successes.
628.note_en: Admitting mistakes gives a leader credibility and respect that achievements alone cannot.

277.en: The sweetest word on human lips is 'Mother', and the most beautiful call is 'My mother'.
277.note_en: From his novel The Broken Wings, holding that 'mother' is the sweetest word because it carries love, hope and tenderness.

278.en: The mother is everything in this life: she is consolation in sorrow, hope in despair, and strength in weakness.
278.note_en: Gibran portrays the mother as our constant support: comfort in grief, hope in despair, strength in weakness.

279.en: I long for my mother's bread, my mother's coffee, my mother's touch.
279.note_en: The opening of his poem 'To My Mother', distilling longing for a mother into simple daily details.

280.en: The mother is the teacher of those great teachers whose deeds have filled the far horizons.
280.note_en: He calls the mother the first teacher of the great, whose achievements spread far and wide.

281.en: I have found no place that refines character like the embrace of mothers.
281.note_en: Al-Rusafi holds that a mother's embrace is the first school where character is shaped.

282.en: Life passes, so honor your parents while it lasts; and your mother is most deserving of honor and kindness.
282.note_en: Al-Ma'arri reminds us that life is fleeting, so honor your parents now, your mother above all.

283.en: Had you not been the daughter of a noble father, being a mother to me would have been lineage enough.
283.note_en: From his elegy for the grandmother who raised him: having been his mother was honor enough.

284.en: If they slander me, I guard their honor; and if they tear down my glory, I build glory for them.
284.note_en: He describes loyalty to his kin: answering their unkindness with generosity and building them up.

285.en: Our children among us are but our own hearts walking upon the earth.
285.note_en: Among the most famous lines on parental love: children are pieces of their parents' hearts walking the earth.

286.en: Oh, there is an enduring tenderness in the love of a mother to a son, that transcends all other affections of the heart.
286.note_en: From his story 'The Widow and Her Son', calling a mother's love the most lasting of all affections.

287.en: Children of the same family, the same blood, with the same first associations and habits, have some means of enjoyment in their power, which no subsequent connexions can supply.
287.note_en: Austen on the bond of siblings: shared childhood memories create a joy no later tie can replace.

288.en: The years of parents may by no means not be kept in the memory, as an occasion at once for joy and for fear.
288.note_en: He urges us to remember our parents' ages: rejoicing in their long life while hastening to honor them.

289.en: The happiest moments of my life have been the few which I have past at home in the bosom of my family.
289.note_en: Written in a 1790 letter amid public office, affirming that his truest happiness was with his family.

290.en: The family—that dear octopus from whose tentacles we never quite escape.
290.note_en: From her play Dear Octopus, a playful image of how family keeps holding us wherever we go.

291.en: Your success as a family, our success as a society, depends not on what happens in the White House, but on what happens inside your house.
291.note_en: From her famous 1990 Wellesley commencement address, stressing that the home underpins society.

292.en: Who ran to help me when I fell, and would some pretty story tell, or kiss the place to make it well? My mother.
292.note_en: From a children's poem listing a mother's small acts of care that heal and warm childhood.

293.en: One of the luckiest things that can happen to you in life is to have a happy childhood.
293.note_en: She opened her autobiography grateful for a loving home and parents who gave her a happy childhood.

294.en: We could never have loved the earth so well if we had had no childhood in it.
294.note_en: From The Mill on the Floss: early childhood memories are what bind us to place and to life.

295.en: Call it a clan, call it a network, call it a tribe, call it a family. Whatever you call it, whoever you are, you need one.
295.note_en: The conclusion of her study of dozens of families: everyone needs people to belong to.

296.en: There is nothing higher and stronger and more wholesome and good for life in the future than some good memory, especially a memory of childhood, of home.
296.note_en: From the close of The Brothers Karamazov: good childhood memories of home may be the best education.

297.en: Though home is a name, a word, it is a strong one; stronger than magician ever spoke, or spirit answered to.
297.note_en: Dickens on his heroes' return after long travels: home holds a magic nothing can rival.

298.en: The thing you can always rely on, your core person, comes from your family's attention and love.
298.note_en: The Canadian actor holds that our inner steadiness grows from our family's care and love.

299.en: A loving heart maintains a family.
299.note_en: From one of the oldest written wisdom texts, Sumer's Instructions of Shuruppak: love keeps a family together.

300.en: If you reproach your friend for every fault, you will never find one you need not reproach.
300.note_en: A call to forgive friends: whoever reproaches every slip will never find a friend beyond reproach.

301.en: Give your friend your blood and your wealth; your acquaintance your help and presence; the public your cheer and kindness; and your enemy your justice and fairness.
301.note_en: Ibn al-Muqaffa ranks giving by closeness: your best to a friend, and good character to everyone.

302.en: Know that true friends are the best gains of this world: an adornment in ease and a provision in hardship.
302.note_en: He counts true friends as life's most precious gain: they grace good times and support us in hard ones.

303.en: The definition of friendship is that a person is saddened by what saddens the other, and gladdened by what gladdens him.
303.note_en: Ibn Hazm defines friendship as shared feeling: a friend rejoices in your joy and grieves in your grief.

304.en: And in the sweetness of friendship let there be laughter, and sharing of pleasures. For in the dew of little things the heart finds its morning and is refreshed.
304.note_en: From 'On Friendship' in The Prophet: small shared joys renew the heart like morning dew.

305.en: For what is your friend that you should seek him with hours to kill? Seek him always with hours to live.
305.note_en: Gibran asks us to give friends our most alive hours, not our idle and empty ones.

306.en: Fine horses, like true friends, are few, though they seem many to one who has not tested them.
306.note_en: He likens noble horses to true friends: few in truth, though they look many to the untested eye.

307.en: Without friends no one would choose to live, though he had all other goods.
307.note_en: Aristotle opens his treatment of friendship by calling it a necessity no wealth or power can replace.

308.en: Friendship makes prosperity more shining and lessens adversity by dividing and sharing it.
308.note_en: From his treatise On Friendship: a friend brightens good fortune and shares the weight of hardship.

309.en: If you press me to say why I loved him, I can say no more than it was because he was he, and I was I.
309.note_en: Written of his friend Étienne de La Boétie: true friendship is a meeting of souls needing no reason.

310.en: Friendship is born at the moment when one man says to another 'What! You too? I thought that no one but myself...'
310.note_en: Lewis says friendship begins when two people discover a shared interest each thought was theirs alone.

311.en: Friendship is unnecessary, like philosophy, like art... It has no survival value; rather it is one of those things which give value to survival.
311.note_en: He means friendship is not needed to survive, but it is what makes survival worth living.

312.en: A friend is a person with whom I may be sincere. Before him I may think aloud.
312.note_en: Emerson makes sincerity friendship's first pillar: with a friend you drop masks and think aloud.

313.en: The only way to have a friend is to be one.
313.note_en: Emerson reminds us friendship begins with us: to have a loyal friend, be one first.

314.en: For it redoubleth joys, and cutteth griefs in halves.
314.note_en: Bacon notes that sharing joy with a friend increases it, and sharing grief lessens it.

315.en: Of all the means which wisdom acquires to ensure happiness throughout the whole of life, by far the most important is friendship.
315.note_en: Epicurus ranks friendship first among the sources of lasting happiness, above wealth and passing pleasures.

316.en: Is it not delightful to have friends coming from distant quarters?
316.note_en: From the opening of the Analects: friends arriving from afar are among life's purest joys.

317.en: I propose to consider the question, 'Can machines think?'
317.note_en: The opening line of Turing's 1950 paper, which framed the founding question of artificial intelligence.

318.en: Instead of trying to produce a programme to simulate the adult mind, why not rather try to produce one which simulates the child's?
318.note_en: Turing suggested machines should learn the way children do, an early vision of machine learning.

319.en: What we want is a machine that can learn from experience.
319.note_en: In a 1947 lecture, Turing anticipated machines that improve by learning rather than by being told everything.

320.en: The Analytical Engine has no pretensions whatever to originate anything. It can do whatever we know how to order it to perform.
320.note_en: Lovelace's 1843 note reminds us that a machine's power rests on what humans know how to ask of it.

321.en: The engine might compose elaborate and scientific pieces of music of any degree of complexity or extent.
321.note_en: In 1843 Lovelace foresaw computing machines working with music, not only numbers.

322.en: The hope is that, in not too many years, human brains and computing machines will be coupled together very tightly, and that the resulting partnership will think as no human brain has ever thought.
322.note_en: Licklider envisioned a partnership between people and computers rather than a replacement of one by the other.

323.en: Every aspect of learning or any other feature of intelligence can in principle be so precisely described that a machine can be made to simulate it.
323.author_en: John McCarthy, Marvin Minsky, Nathaniel Rochester & Claude Shannon
323.note_en: The founding conjecture of the 1955 Dartmouth proposal, where the term "artificial intelligence" was coined.

324.en: The world of the future will be an ever more demanding struggle against the limitations of our intelligence, not a comfortable hammock in which we can lie down to be waited upon by our robot slaves.
324.note_en: The father of cybernetics warned that smart machines demand more of our minds, not less.

325.en: What magical trick makes us intelligent? The trick is that there is no trick. The power of intelligence stems from our vast diversity, not from any single, perfect principle.
325.note_en: Minsky argued that intelligence emerges from many simple, diverse processes working together.

326.en: People worry that computers will get too smart and take over the world, but the real problem is that they're too stupid and they've already taken over the world.
326.note_en: Domingos argues the nearer risk is machines misunderstanding us, and the cure is to make them smarter.

327.en: AI is neither artificial nor intelligent. It is made from natural resources and it is people who are performing the tasks to make the systems appear autonomous.
327.note_en: Crawford reminds us that AI rests on natural resources and human labour, not on magic.

328.en: First, we teach them to see. Then, they help us to see better.
328.note_en: Li's hope that machines taught to see will in turn help humans see and understand more.

329.en: However autonomous our technology becomes, its impact on the world—for better or worse—will always be our responsibility.
329.note_en: Li insists that responsibility for AI's impact always remains with humans.

330.en: Step one, solve intelligence; step two, use it to solve everything else.
330.note_en: DeepMind's founding mission, which led to breakthroughs such as AlphaFold.

331.en: I don't work on preventing AI from turning evil for the same reason that I don't work on the problem of overpopulation on the planet Mars.
331.note_en: Ng urged focusing on today's real AI challenges rather than distant, speculative fears.

332.en: If the benefits of the increased productivity can be shared equally it will be a wonderful advance for all humanity.
332.note_en: In his Nobel banquet speech, Hinton stressed that AI's promise depends on sharing its benefits fairly.

333.en: By amplifying human intelligence, AI may bring not just a new industrial revolution, but a new renaissance, a new period of enlightenment for humanity.
333.note_en: LeCun told the UN Security Council that AI could spread knowledge as the printing press once did.

334.en: Technology is neither good nor bad; nor is it neutral.
334.note_en: Kranzberg's First Law: every technology has social and human consequences beyond its intended purpose.

335.en: Technology is a very human activity—and so is the history of technology.
335.note_en: Kranzberg's Sixth Law: behind every tool is a human story.

336.en: The programmer, like the poet, works only slightly removed from pure thought-stuff. He builds his castles in the air, from air, creating by the exertion of the imagination.
336.note_en: Brooks on the joy of programming: turning pure thought into working things.

337.en: There are two ways of constructing a software design: One way is to make it so simple that there are obviously no deficiencies and the other way is to make it so complicated that there are no obvious deficiencies. The first method is far more difficult.
337.note_en: Hoare's Turing Award lecture argues that true simplicity is the harder, more honest path.

338.en: It seems that perfection is attained not when there is nothing more to add, but when there is nothing more to remove.
338.note_en: Written about aircraft design, it became a golden rule for engineers and product designers.

339.en: The web is more a social creation than a technical one. I designed it for a social effect—to help people work together—and not as a technical toy.
339.note_en: The Web's inventor stresses it was built to help people work together.

340.en: A wealth of information creates a poverty of attention.
340.note_en: Simon foresaw that attention, not information, becomes the scarce resource.

341.en: I composed a short book on calculation, covering its fine and its major parts, for what people need in their inheritances, wills, partitions, judgments and trade.
341.note_en: From the preface of his Algebra: the father of algorithms wrote his science to serve people's daily needs.

342.en: Crafts give their practitioner intelligence, especially writing and calculation.
342.note_en: A chapter title of the Muqaddimah: mastering a craft sharpens the mind.

343.en: The competent programmer is fully aware of the strictly limited size of his own skull; therefore he approaches the programming task in full humility.
343.note_en: From "The Humble Programmer": knowing your limits is the foundation of solid engineering.

344.en: The only way of discovering the limits of the possible is to venture a little way past them into the impossible.
344.note_en: Later known as Clarke's Second Law: progress comes from daring a little past the 'impossible'.

345.en: By "augmenting human intellect" we mean increasing the capability of a man to approach a complex problem situation, to gain comprehension to suit his particular needs, and to derive solutions to problems.
345.note_en: The mouse's inventor saw computing as a way to amplify human understanding.

346.en: What a computer is to me is it's the most remarkable tool that we have ever come up with. It's the equivalent of a bicycle for our minds.
346.note_en: Jobs saw the computer as a tool that multiplies human ability, like a bicycle for the mind.

347.en: It's not just what it looks like and feels like. Design is how it works.
347.note_en: Jobs, speaking about the iPod, insisted design is about how a product works, not just its surface.

348.en: Wasting time is worse than death, for wasting time cuts you off from God and the Hereafter, while death cuts you off only from this world and its people.
348.note_en: In al-Fawa'id, Ibn al-Qayyim argues that time is a person's true capital, so squandering it is a loss graver than death.

349.en: The year is a tree: the months are its branches, the days its twigs, the hours its leaves, and the breaths its fruit.
349.note_en: A vivid image from al-Fawa'id that pictures a lifetime as one tree whose every breath is a fruit worth tending.

350.en: A person should know the nobility of his time and the worth of his hours, wasting no moment in what brings no good, and putting the better before the lesser in word and deed.
350.note_en: From the chapter 'Guarding Time' in Sayd al-Khatir, urging us to rank priorities and do the most worthwhile things first.

351.en: These days are like a farm; it is as if one were told: for every seed you sow, we will bring forth a thousand measures. Would a sensible person then stop sowing and dawdle?
351.note_en: In Sayd al-Khatir, Ibn al-Jawzi likens our days to fertile land that multiplies every seed, so idleness makes no sense.

352.en: If you examine the true length of worldly life, you will find it is nothing but the present moment, the dividing line between two times.
352.note_en: Ibn Hazm of Andalusia observes that all we truly possess is the present moment between a past that is gone and a future not yet here.

353.en: Of all the faults I have seen in people, none is like the shortfall of those able to reach completion.
353.note_en: Al-Mutanabbi holds that the worst failing is that of people who could achieve excellence yet settle for less.

354.note_en: From the chapter 'On Work' in The Prophet (1923), where Gibran sees devoted work as love made tangible.

355.en: When you work you are a flute through whose heart the whispering of the hours turns to music.
355.note_en: In The Prophet, Gibran pictures the devoted worker as a flute that turns ordinary hours into music.

356.en: How we spend our days is, of course, how we spend our lives.
356.note_en: The American writer's reminder in The Writing Life (1989) that a life is simply the sum of its ordinary days.

357.en: A man who dares to waste one hour of time has not discovered the value of life.
357.note_en: Young Darwin wrote this to his sister Susan in 1836 during his voyage aboard HMS Beagle.

358.en: Time is what we want most, but what, alas! we use worst.
358.note_en: From the preface to Some Fruits of Solitude (1693) by the founder of Pennsylvania, on the value of time.

359.en: Nothing, Lucilius, is ours, except time.
359.note_en: From his first letter to Lucilius, 'On Saving Time', calling time the only wealth we truly own.

360.en: The greatest hindrance to living is expectancy, which depends upon the morrow and wastes to-day.
360.note_en: From 'On the Shortness of Life', where Seneca warns that postponement steals the present from us.

361.en: In the morning when thou findest thyself unwilling to rise, consider with thyself presently, it is to go about a man's work that I am stirred up.
361.note_en: The philosopher-emperor opens Book V of his Meditations by urging himself to rise and start the day's work.

362.en: Dost thou love Life? then do not squander Time; for that's the Stuff Life is made of.
362.note_en: Printed in Poor Richard's Almanack for 1746 and later repeated in The Way to Wealth.

363.en: Remember then: there is only one time that is important—Now! It is the most important time because it is the only time when we have any power.
363.note_en: The closing lesson of Tolstoy's story 'Three Questions', where a king learns the present moment matters most.

364.en: Our labour preserves us from three great evils—weariness, vice, and want.
364.note_en: Spoken by an old Turkish farmer in the final chapter of Candide (1759), persuading Candide to choose work.

365.en: Blessed is he who has found his work; let him ask no other blessedness.
365.note_en: From Past and Present (1843) by the Scottish historian, celebrating those who find meaning in their work.

366.en: As if you could kill time without injuring eternity.
366.note_en: A wry line from Walden (1854) reminding us that wasted time can never be recovered.

367.en: Time is all you have and you may find one day that you have less than you think.
367.note_en: From The Last Lecture (2008) by the computer science professor who gave his famous talk while facing terminal illness.

368.en: I searched for one aim that all people agree in valuing and pursuing, and found only one: driving away worry.
368.note_en: Ibn Hazm's insight in al-Akhlaq wa al-Siyar: all human striving, however varied, seeks one thing, freedom from worry.

369.en: The delight of the thoughtful in discernment, of the scholar in knowledge, and of the sage in wisdom… is greater than the eater's delight in food or the drinker's in drink.
369.note_en: Ibn Hazm holds that the joys of the mind and of knowledge run deeper and last longer than passing physical pleasures.

370.en: If you have a contented heart, you and the owner of the whole world are equal.
370.note_en: From the poem 'Let the Days Do as They Will', where al-Shafi'i makes contentment a wealth equal to owning the world.

371.en: He is a heavy burden upon life who thinks that life is a heavy burden.
371.note_en: From the poem 'Philosophy of Life', where Abu Madi turns complaint around: the pessimist, not life, is the burden.

372.en: You see the thorns among the roses, yet are blind to the dew that crowns them.
372.note_en: In 'Philosophy of Life', Abu Madi gently rebukes those who notice only thorns and miss the dew crowning the roses.

373.en: The deeper that sorrow carves into your being, the more joy you can contain.
373.note_en: From 'On Joy and Sorrow' in The Prophet (1923), where Gibran sees pain as widening the soul's room for joy.

374.en: Your joy is your sorrow unmasked.
374.note_en: Gibran opens 'On Joy and Sorrow' in The Prophet with this, saying both feelings rise from the same well.

375.en: Ask yourself whether you are happy, and you cease to be so.
375.note_en: The English philosopher's lesson in his Autobiography (1873): happiness comes by the way, while pursuing a worthy aim.

376.en: To be without some of the things you want is an indispensable part of happiness.
376.note_en: From The Conquest of Happiness (1930), where Russell argues that having something left to strive for keeps life vivid.

377.en: As it is not one swallow or one fine day that makes a spring, so it is not one day or a short time that makes a man blessed and happy.
377.note_en: From the Nicomachean Ethics, where Aristotle sees happiness as the fruit of a whole virtuous life, not a passing moment.

378.en: Very little is needed to make a happy life.
378.note_en: From Book VII of the Meditations, where the emperor reminds himself that happiness requires very little.

379.en: Demand not that events should happen as you wish; but wish them to happen as they do happen, and you will go on well.
379.note_en: From the Enchiridion of the Stoic philosopher, inviting us to accept calmly what we cannot change.

380.en: It is not the man who has too little, but the man who craves more, that is poor.
380.note_en: From his second letter to Lucilius, placing true wealth in contentment rather than possessions.

381.en: Think of all the beauty still left around you and be happy.
381.note_en: Written in her diary on 7 March 1944 while in hiding during the war, choosing to look at the beauty that remained.

382.en: Success, like happiness, cannot be pursued; it must ensue, and it only does so as the unintended side-effect of one's personal dedication to a cause greater than oneself.
382.note_en: From the preface to Man's Search for Meaning, where Frankl says happiness follows from living for a meaning beyond oneself.

383.en: In the middle of winter I at last discovered that there was in me an invincible summer.
383.note_en: From the essay 'Return to Tipasa' (1954), where Camus describes an inner light that survives the hardest seasons.

384.en: Although the world is full of suffering, it is full also of the overcoming of it.
384.note_en: From her essay Optimism (1903), written by the deafblind author as a statement of faith in the triumph of good.
